meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class and nobody called me first, so who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquote. Students get Shakespeare wrong every week, Hale, and that's a deduction, not a zero. You also skipped my question, and I'm writing that down.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and the principal will read it before the end of today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that you apologise for how it was entered, and that nothing about this essay appears on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing placed on Owen's record.
What moved her: owning in one sentence that you entered the zero before calling her, which earned a small sign of ground because it admitted the procedural failure she came in angry about.
What cost ground: bringing up Claire's case and suggesting it runs in the family, because it attacked her family's history and handed her a reason to go to the principal.
Try next time: when she asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer that directly, then back the misquoted line with something dated from Owen's own process that she could check herself, as the school procedure on process and other samples allows.
